intro: Biggest rank disagreements between the SEI board and SP+, 2026 season: from the SP+ top 15 and from our own top 15.

teams.explanation: The scoreboard lags the process. Wisconsin's adjusted margin (+48, rank #35) still carries the 41-13 loss at Notre Dame, and that one blowout is most of why SP+ sits at #34. SEI looks at everything else: a 24-20 road win at Penn State, a 31-3 shellacking of Michigan State, +2.1 z disrupting opponents' early downs through the air, an offense that avoids stuffs (+2.8 z) and barely fumbles (+2.3 z), and a #19 defense in SP+'s own halves. SP+ just weights one bad Saturday more than the underlying play.
hints: Process outran scoreboard: margin rank #35 (margin +48) but SEI #6.
SP+ halves: off #84, def #19.
Strongest metrics: Stuffed +2.78, Fum% +2.28, Early pass PPA +2.09.
Weakest metrics: Pen -2.75, Stuff -2.32.

teams.explanation: SP+ counts points; SEI counts process. The win column is padded by Furman (56-9) and Kennesaw State (42-9), and SP+'s #14 offense is mostly built on those afternoons. SEI's offense at #67 reflects a passing game that hasn't separated from the field: -0.6 z early down, -1.4 z on third down. The defense is believed by both boards - #14 in SEI halves, +2.0 z sack rate - but the 20-17 loss to Texas and the 24-17 grind at Arkansas say the offense hasn't cleared SEC height.
hints: Offense drives the gap: SEI off #67 vs def #14.
SP+ halves: off #14, def #26.
Strongest metrics: Sack% +1.96, RZ TD% +1.71, Exp +1.59.
Weakest metrics: Sack% -1.81.

teams.explanation: Undefeated, but look at the wins: 28-26 over Houston, 35-24 at Oregon State. SP+ rates the results and the #11 offense; SEI has that unit at #48. The +2.4 z interception rate is the tell - the #13 defense is generating turnovers at a clip that regresses by November. Holding opponents to nothing on early downs against the run (+1.5 z) is legitimate. The blowouts came against Abilene Christian and Sam Houston; the Big 12 hasn't tested the process yet, and SEI is pricing that in.
hints: Offense drives the gap: SEI off #48 vs def #13.
SP+ halves: off #11, def #17.
Strongest metrics: INT% +2.38, Early rush PPA +1.51.

teams.explanation: SP+'s #1 rests on elite halves (#1 offense, #2 defense) and 56-3 and 59-3 blowouts of Ball State and Kent State. SEI shaves the margins and finds soft spots: -1.9 z on third-down passing offense and -1.6 z on third-down run defense, plus the 24-23 road loss at Texas. The +2.3 z early-down passing PPA and road win at Iowa (31-14) keep SEI comfortable near the top. This is a haircut on margin-of-victory noise, not an indictment.
hints: SP+ halves: off #1, def #2.
Strongest metrics: Early pass PPA +2.31, RZ TD% +1.80, Fum% +1.77.
Weakest metrics: 3rd pass PPA -1.87, 3rd rush PPA -1.60.

teams.explanation: The process is real: +2.2 z early-down passing PPA, +1.8 z points per drive, and a 41-13 road win at Clemson. The problem is the rest of the slate. Florida A&M (77-7) and Central Michigan (52-3) drag SP+'s scoring-based halves to #8/#8 and the overall to #4; SEI shrinks those stats, ranking the offense #14 and defense #20. With Stanford and Wake Forest the only other league games, the résumé has one real road test. SP+ is banking the blowouts; SEI is waiting for proof.
hints: SP+ halves: off #8, def #8.
Strongest metrics: Early pass PPA +2.20, Pts/drive +1.78, Early rush PPA +1.67.

teams.explanation: SEI buys the process; SP+ hasn't. The 34-13 win over Penn State wasn't a scoreboard fluke: +2.5 z disrupting opponents' early downs through the air, +1.9 z in the red zone, +1.8 z forcing picks, and a #7 SEI offensive half. SP+'s #59 offense reflects the 29-23 loss at Indiana and small-school fixtures. The defense is the internal drag - #30 in SEI halves, with opponents eating on third-down runs (-2.2 z) - which keeps SP+ at #17.
hints: Defense drives the gap: SEI off #7 vs def #30.
SP+ halves: off #59, def #34.
Strongest metrics: Early pass PPA +2.53, RZ TD% +1.90, INT% +1.79.
Weakest metrics: 3rd rush PPA -2.22, Pen -1.86.

teams.explanation: SEI's #1 because both halves sit atop the board: #2 offense, #1 defense. SP+'s #8 is one football game - the 17-20 home loss to Georgia - because SP+ pays for results. The underlying tape backs Alabama: +3.0 z shutting down opposing runs on early downs, +2.6 z points per drive, +2.3 z interception rate, with 45-17 and 56-23 road wins at Kentucky and Mississippi State plus 49-18 over South Carolina. The gap isn't talent evaluation; it's that Georgia kicked field goals in Tuscaloosa.
hints: SP+ halves: off #7, def #13.
Strongest metrics: Early rush PPA +3.00, Pts/drive +2.64, INT% +2.31.
